characterization_methods.key_findings: Slight decrease in yield strength with increasing solution temperature attributed to grain growth; work-hardening rate ordering (6Al highest to 12Al lowest) retained after the 1100 °C treatment.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ambient temperature; initial strain rate 1.1 × 10^-3 s^-1; round specimens (gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm) cut with tensile axis parallel to the rod axis
characterization_methods.purpose: To measure yield strength, tensile strength, elongation and work-hardening behaviour of the Al-series (incl. Al-10) after 1100 °C/2 h solution treatment (Fig. 2d, Fig. 8d).
characterization_methods.technique: uniaxial tensile testing (engineering stress-strain, true stress-strain and work-hardening rate)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD system attached to a field emission gun scanning electron microscope (FEI Quanta 650, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Hillsboro, OR, USA)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: operating voltage 20 kV, step size 0.5 μm; specimens electro-polished in 7% Nital at room temperature; grain size by linear intercept with 15° misorientation criterion (Channel 5 software)
characterization_methods.purpose: To determine phase distribution and grain size of the solution-treated low-density steels (Table 3). In this work the EBSD maps (Figs. 3-5) were acquired on the 1050 °C solution-treated series; the 1100 °C sample of the present extraction was not EBSD-characterised.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM, Tecnai G2 F20 S-TWIN, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Hillsboro, OR, USA
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: operated at 200 kV; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in 10% perchloric acid + 90% ethanol at 20 V and −20 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: To examine κ-carbide precipitation (size, distribution, orientation relationship) in the solution-treated steels (Figs. 3-5); applied to the 1050 °C series, not to the present 1100 °C sample.
characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM, bright-field and dark-field, with SAED)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength (slight decrease with increasing solution treatment temperature, attributed to increased grain size)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Each steel composition was first melted in a high-frequency vacuum induction furnace with a 50 kg capacity, then cast into an ingot with a diameter of 150 mm.
The resulting ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h.
Hot rolled into rods with a diameter of 16 mm, before being air-cooled to room temperature.

As-distinct terminal state for this sample: specimens with different Al content (including Al-10) were solution treated at 1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching, applied to assess the effect of solution temperature (Fig. 2d, Fig. 8d).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Two solution-treated specimens tested; data is the average value of two specimens.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: round tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm, tensile axis parallel to the rod axis

strain_hardening_rate: True stress-strain and work-hardening-rate curves for the Al-series after 1100 °C solution treatment are given in Fig. 8(d); the work-hardening rate decreases with increasing Al content (6Al highest, 12Al lowest) and the response is similar to that after 1050 °C.
tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curves of the Al-series (6-12% Al) after 1100 °C/2 h solution treatment + WQ are shown in Fig. 2(d); a slight decrease in yield strength is observed relative to the 1050 °C treatment, attributed to increased grain size.

structures.overall_structure: Al-10 (Fe30Mn10Al1C) after 1100 °C/2 h solution treatment + water quenching. Raising the solution-treatment temperature to 1100 °C increased the grain size (grain growth), which the authors proposed as the cause of the slight decrease in yield strength relative to the 1050 °C treatment. The 1100 °C samples were used only to compare the solution-temperature effect (Fig. 2d, Fig. 8d) and were not characterised by EBSD/TEM, so the phase constitution and grain size are not reported for this state.

unmapped_findings: Data for the Al-10 (Fe30Mn10Al1C) alloy in the 1050 °C/2 h solution-treated state — NOT this 1100 °C sample — are: UTS 830 ± 0 MPa, YS 642 ± 2 MPa, uniform elongation 72 ± 2.8%, total elongation 73.5 ± 1%, and Charpy impact toughness 237 ± 5 J at −40 °C (Table 2, row Al-10). These values belong to the 1050 °C state and must not be assigned to the 1100 °C sample.

The 1050 °C/2 h solution-treated Al-10 microstructure (Table 3, block b0047) is: single austenite phase, D_FCC-G/T = 29.7 ± 1.1 μm, twin-boundary fraction f_Tw = 53.2%, no ferrite (f_Bcc and D_Bcc not reported), κ-carbide diameter 1.0 ± 0.4 nm. These microstructural values correspond to the 1050 °C state, not to this 1100 °C sample.

For the present 1100 °C sample the paper reports only that the yield strength slightly decreases with increasing solution-treatment temperature relative to the 1050 °C values (Fig. 2d), attributed to increased grain size; no numeric tensile values are tabulated for the 1100 °C state.

For the 1100 °C Al-series solution treatment, work-hardening rate curves (Fig. 8d) retain the ordering 6Al highest → 12Al lowest; the stress-strain curves extend to noticeably larger true strain than at 1050 °C; σ_TS and σ_FS are reported as not varying significantly with C, Mn and Al after 1050 °C or 1100 °C treatment.

Density as a function of alloying content: ρ = 8.10 − 0.102C − 0.10Al − 0.01Mn g/cm³ (Eq. 3; C, Al, Mn in mass%), which predicts 6.6 g/cm³ for Fe30Mn11Al1.0C matching experiment; this is a general relation for the FeMnAlC series rather than a value specific to this sample (blocks b0063, b0081; figure_unlabelled_008).

General (not sample-specific) κ-carbide strengthening relations derived in the paper: σ_shear = α f^(1/2) d_Car^(1/2) (Eq. 4), with fitted slope 97.1 MPa/nm^(1/2) and a flow stress in the absence of κ-carbides of about 478 MPa (Fig. 7a, blocks b0069, b0071); σ_TS ≈ 1350 MPa and σ_FS ≈ 2150 MPa for all investigated compositions (block b0080).

The paper's conclusion (block b0082) states an excellent combination of yield strength 642 MPa, ductility 72% and impact toughness at −40 °C of 247 J at density 6.69 g/cm³ was obtained for Fe30Mn10Al1C after 1050 °C solution treatment; note this toughness value (247 J) differs slightly from the 237 J listed for Al-10 in Table 2 (block b0033).

Charpy impact toughness specimens were cut with the V-notch perpendicular to the rod axis and tested with an MTS impact tester (500 J capacity) at −40 °C (block b0017); impact results are reported for the 1050 °C solution-treated series and no impact data are reported for the 1100 °C state of this sample.
